column1: judicious§A judicious editor cut four chapters and left the book shorter, sharper, and considerably more likely to be finished.§一位**明智的**编辑砍掉四章，让这本书更短、更锋利，也更可能被读完。§judic（判断，同 judge 法官）
juxtapose§The exhibition juxtaposes the plans with the photographs, and the gap between them is the whole argument.§这个展览把图纸与照片**并置**，两者之间的落差就是全部论点。§juxta（靠近）+ pos（放置，同 position 位置）
juxtaposition§The juxtaposition of the two dates on one page tells you more than four pages of commentary could.§一页上两个日期的**并列**告诉你的，比四页评注还多。§
kinetic§The sculpture is kinetic, and half its meaning disappears in a photograph that cannot show it moving.§这件雕塑是**动态的**，照片拍不出它的运动，它一半的意味也就消失了。§
knack§The knack takes about nine hours to acquire and, once acquired, cannot be explained to anyone else.§这项**诀窍**大约要九小时才学得会，学会之后又没法向别人解释。§
knowledgeable§The most knowledgeable person about the site was the caretaker, and nobody interviewed him until 2004.§对这处遗址最**熟悉了解的**是看管人，而直到 2004 年才有人采访他。§
lackadaisical§Their lackadaisical approach to the paperwork cost them a permit and, with it, an entire building season.§他们对文书工作**懒散敷衍的**态度让他们丢了许可，也丢了整个施工季。§源自叹词 lackaday（唉，可叹）
laconic§His laconic reply—two words, "Not yet"—became the single most quoted sentence of a four-hour public hearing.§他那句**简短的**回答，两个字「还没」，成了长达四小时公开听证会上被引用最多的一句。§Laconia（斯巴达所在地，人以言简著称）
lament§She laments the loss of the archive in an essay that is itself the best record of what it held.§她在一篇文章里**哀叹**档案的散失，而这篇文章本身是其内容最好的记录。§lament（哭泣）
languid§The afternoon was languid until a phone call emptied the office in about ninety seconds.§那个下午一直**懒洋洋的**，直到一通电话在约九十秒内清空了办公室。§langu（虚弱，同 languish 憔悴）
languor§A languor settled over the town in August, and nothing was decided until the schools reopened.§八月里一种**倦怠**笼罩了这座小镇，直到学校重开才有事情被决定。§
lassitude§The lassitude after the illness lasted four months, and it worried her more than the fever had.§病后的**倦怠无力**持续了四个月，比发烧更让她担心。§lassus（疲乏）
latent§The fault was latent for eleven years and surfaced the first time the building took a real load.§这个缺陷**潜伏**了十一年，在建筑首次承受真实荷载时才显现。§lat（隐藏）
laud§Critics lauded the restoration, and the conservator who did it has never been named in any of the reviews.§评论界**盛赞**这次修复，而做修复的文物保护师在任何评论里都未被提及。§laud（赞美）
lavish§The firm was lavish with the launch party and stingy with the salaries, and the staff noticed both.§这家公司在发布派对上**大手大脚**，在薪水上小气，员工两样都看在眼里。§
lavishly§The building was lavishly decorated and cheaply built, and the second fact showed up within nine years.§这栋楼装修**奢华**而建造廉价，第二点在九年内就暴露了。§
lax§Security was lax for four years, and the first serious breach was reported by a visitor.§安保**松懈**了四年，第一次严重的漏洞是一位访客报告的。§lax（松，同 relax 放松）
leery§Investors are leery of the sector after four failures, and the fifth company cannot raise anything at all.§四次失败后投资人对这个行业**心存戒备**，第五家公司完全融不到钱。§
legalize§Nine states legalized the practice within four years, and the predicted collapse in standards never appeared.§九个州在四年内将这一做法**合法化**，而预言中的标准崩塌从未出现。§leg（法律，同 legal 法律的）
legendary§His patience with beginners was legendary, and four of his students now run departments of their own.§他对初学者的耐心**堪称传奇**，他的四名学生如今各自主持着系。§leg（读）
legitimacy§The government's legitimacy rested on an election that nine international observers refused to certify.§这个政府的**合法性**建立在一场九名国际观察员拒绝认证的选举之上。§
legitimate§The concern is legitimate and the remedy proposed is not, which is why the debate has gone nowhere.§这个担忧是**正当的**而提出的补救办法不是，所以争论毫无进展。§leg（法律，同 legal 法律的）
legitimize§Publishing the figures legitimized a practice that had survived for years precisely by staying unmeasured.§公布这些数字让一种恰恰靠不被测量而存续多年的做法**取得了正当性**。§
lengthy§The lengthy preamble discourages most readers from ever reaching the four paragraphs that actually matter.§**冗长的**前言劝退了多数读者，让他们根本读不到真正要紧的那四段。§
leniency§Leniency in the first case established an expectation that made the second one impossible to punish.§第一起案件的**宽大**建立了一种预期，使得第二起无法惩处。§
lessen§Nothing lessened the noise until the road was resurfaced, and the council had refused that for nine years.§在路面重铺之前什么也不能**减轻**噪音，而议会拒绝这么做已有九年。§
lethargy§The lethargy that followed the announcement lasted three weeks, and no work of any kind got done.§公告之后的**萎靡不振**持续三周，任何工作都没做成。§lethe（遗忘）+ argia（不动）
levity§A little levity would have helped, and the speaker maintained the same grave tone for forty minutes.§一点**轻松诙谐**本会有帮助，而演讲者用同样凝重的语调讲了四十分钟。§lev（轻，同 elevate 抬起）
levy§The council levied a charge on empty properties, and nine of the eleven were occupied within a year.§议会对空置房产**征收**费用，十一处中有九处一年内住上了人。§lev（举起，同 elevate 抬起）→ 把税抬起来收
lexicon§The lexicon of the trade takes about a year to learn, and outsiders never quite stop sounding wrong.§这一行的**词汇**约需一年学会，而外人怎么说都还是有点不对。§
liability§The old building is a liability rather than an asset: it costs more to insure than it would to replace.§这栋老楼是**负担**而非资产——保险费比重建费还高。§li（捆绑，同 liable 有责任的）
libel§The libel action cost the paper nine hundred thousand pounds and confirmed every fact it had printed.§这场**诽谤**官司让报社花了九十万英镑，却证实了它刊登的每一个事实。§
liberality§The liberality of the terms surprised everyone, and it turned out to be the cheapest way to end the dispute.§条件的**宽厚**让所有人意外，而它原来是结束纠纷最便宜的办法。§liber（自由，同 liberty 自由）
libertine§The libertine of the first four chapters becomes, without explanation, the moralist of the last two.§前四章里的那个**放荡不羁者**，毫无交代地变成了最后两章的道德家。§liber（自由）
licentious§The play was called licentious in 1892 and is taught, uncontroversially, in schools today.§这部剧在 1892 年被称为**伤风败俗的**，如今在学校里教授，毫无争议。§licent（放任，同 license 许可）
likelihood§The likelihood of a repeat is small, and the consequence if it happens is large enough to plan for.§重演的**可能性**很小，而一旦发生后果大到值得预作准备。§
linchpin§The old sorting office was the linchpin of the network, and closing it slowed every route in the region.§那座旧分拣中心是整个网络的**关键**，关闭它拖慢了区内每一条线路。§lynis（车轴）+ pin（销）
linkage§The linkage between the two payments was never written down, and both sides now describe it differently.§这两笔付款之间的**关联**从未落于纸面，如今双方的说法各不相同。§
lionize§London lionized him for one season, and by the next his name appeared in nobody's guest list.§伦敦**追捧**了他一季，到下一季他的名字已不出现在任何人的宾客名单上。§lion（狮子）→ 当名兽一样围观
liquefy§The gas liquefies at four atmospheres, which is what makes it practical to move by ship at all.§这种气体在四个大气压下**液化**，这才使得用船运输成为可能。§liqu（液体，同 liquid 液体）
lithe§The lithe old dancer could still do at seventy what her students found difficult at twenty.§这位**身姿柔韧的**老舞者七十岁还能做到她的学生二十岁觉得难的动作。§
litigious§The company is litigious by policy: it has sued four critics and won against none of them.§这家公司**好打官司**是政策使然——它起诉过四位批评者，一个也没赢。§litig（诉讼，同 litigation 诉讼）
loathe§She loathes the phrase and has struck it out of every document that has crossed her desk in nine years.§她**厌恶**这个说法，九年里经她手的每一份文件都被她划掉了它。§
lobbyist§A single lobbyist wrote four paragraphs that appear, word for word, in the final act.§一位**说客**写的四段文字一字不差地出现在最终法案里。§lobby（游说厅）
locution§The locution is regional, and readers outside the county have consistently misunderstood the sentence.§这个**说法**是地方性的，郡外的读者一直误解那句话。§locut（说，同 eloquent 雄辩的）
loftiness§The loftiness of the tone undercuts an argument that would have been stronger stated plainly.§语调的**高高在上**削弱了一个本可以平实陈述而更有力的论点。§loft（高处）
lone§A lone objector delayed the scheme for four years and was, on the central point, entirely right.§一位**孤单的**反对者把这个方案拖了四年，而在核心问题上他完全正确。§
loner§The loner in the department produced more usable work than the four people who met about it weekly.§系里那位**独来独往的人**做出的有用成果，超过每周为此开会的那四个人。§
longevity§The longevity of the design is remarkable: the same mechanism has been made, almost unchanged, since 1911.§这个设计的**长寿**了不起——同样的机构自 1911 年起几乎原样生产至今。§long（长）+ ev（年岁，同 medieval 中世纪的）
loquacious§The most loquacious member of the panel said the least, and the transcript makes that painfully clear.§评审组里最**话多的**成员说的实质内容最少，文字记录把这点显得刺眼。§loqu（说，同 eloquent 雄辩的）
lucid§Her lucid summary of a nine-hundred-page report saved the committee an entire afternoon of confusion.§她对一份九百页报告**清晰明白的**总结，为委员会省下了整整一下午的困惑。§luc（光，同 lucid 明亮）
lucrative§The side business turned out to be more lucrative than the main one, and by 1998 it was the main one.§这项副业最终比主业更**赚钱**，到 1998 年它就成了主业。§lucr（利益）
ludicrous§The comparison is ludicrous on its face, and it was still repeated without comment in four separate newspapers.§这个类比表面上就**荒唐可笑**，却仍被四家不同的报纸原样转述，未加任何评论。§lud（玩，同 illusion 幻觉）
lugubrious§His lugubrious delivery made a funny script sound like a warning, which the audience found funnier still.§他**哀戚**的表演让一个搞笑剧本听着像警告，观众反而觉得更好笑。§lugubr（哀悼）
lullaby§The lullaby is four hundred years old, and the words nobody sings any more describe a shipwreck.§这首**摇篮曲**有四百年历史，而没人再唱的那些歌词描述的是一场海难。§lull（哄睡）+ bye
lurid§The lurid coverage obscured a story that was, in its ordinary details, far more disturbing.§**耸人听闻的**报道掩盖了一个在寻常细节上更令人不安的故事。§lurid（惨白）
lush§The valley is lush for four months and, once the river drops in July, indistinguishable from desert.§这条河谷有四个月**草木葱茏**，七月河水一落便与沙漠无异。§
luxurious§The carriage was luxurious and slow, and passengers who cared about time took the later, plainer train.§这节车厢**豪华**而缓慢，在意时间的乘客坐了更晚、更朴素的那班车。§lux（奢华）
machination§The machinations took four years to unravel, and the man at the centre of them was never charged.§这些**阴谋**花了四年才理清，而处于核心的那个人从未被起诉。§machin（装置／计谋，同 machine 机器）
magisterial§His magisterial survey of the period is still the standard work, and it is also wrong about four dates.§他对那个时期**权威详尽的**综述至今仍是标准著作，同时它有四个日期是错的。§magistr（长官，同 magistrate 地方官）
magnanimity§The magnanimity of the winner did more for the town than any policy either candidate had proposed.§胜者的**宽宏大量**为这座小镇做的，超过两位候选人提出的任何政策。§magn（大，同 magnify 放大）+ anim（心气，同 animate 赋予生气）
magnanimous§It was magnanimous of her to credit a rival whose objection had, in fact, improved the whole design.§她**宽宏大度**地感谢了一位对手，而那位的反对确实改进了整个设计。§
magnify§The instrument magnifies four hundred times, and at that power a hair looks like a rope.§这台仪器**放大**四百倍，在这个倍率下一根头发看着像绳子。§magn（大）+ fy（使）
magnitude§The magnitude of the loss became clear only when someone converted the figure into years of the department's budget.§损失的**量级**直到有人把数字换算成部门多少年的预算才清楚起来。§magn（大）
mainstay§Rice was the mainstay of the local economy for four centuries and is now grown by nine households.§稻米四个世纪来是当地经济的**支柱**，如今只有九户人家在种。§main（主）+ stay（支索）
malfeasance§The malfeasance was small, systematic, and carried out over eleven years by four people in one office.§这起**渎职**规模不大、成体系，由一个办公室的四个人在十一年间实施。§mal（坏，同 malice 恶意）+ feas（做，同 feasible 可行的）
mandate§The government claimed a mandate for the change and had campaigned on almost the opposite policy.§政府声称改革有**民意授权**，而它竞选时打的几乎是相反的政策。§man（手，同 manual 手工的）+ dat（给，同 date 日期）→ 交到手上的命令
mandatory§Reporting became mandatory in 2011, and the recorded number of incidents promptly tripled without anything else changing.§上报在 2011 年成为**强制性的**，在别无变化的情况下记录在案的事件数量随即增至三倍。§
